source.title: Hessian based analysis of SGD for Deep Nets: Dynamics and Generalization
source.authors: Xinyan Li; Qilong Gu; Yingxue Zhou; Tiancong Chen; Arindam Banerjee

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies SGD dynamics and reports training-loss behavior, but does not measure the training classification error named by any claim version.
record.gate_note: The paper reports loss trajectories and gradient norms, not training classification error. It also cites prior work on over-parameterized networks and random initialization; those cited results are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study's own results concern SGD loss dynamics and Hessian structure in fully connected ReLU networks. They do not test V1's convolutional-network settings, V2's teacher–student width comparison, V3's depth degradation and shortcut comparison, V4's initialization comparisons, V5's stability-threshold behavior, or V6's normalization comparisons. Reporting loss rather than classification error is not alone decisive: cross-entropy approaching zero implies classification error approaching zero, but the tested architectures and datasets still do not match V1.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's convergence paraphrase is broadly accurate but omits central conclusions. The authors report substantial overlap between the leading subspaces of the stochastic-gradient second moment and loss Hessian despite their different spectra; characterize stochastic loss changes with deviation bounds; establish stationary-point convergence under specified adaptive step-size or diagonal-preconditioning assumptions; and derive a scale-invariant PAC-Bayesian generalization bound. They do not report benchmark training classification-error values.
record.recipe_differences: Uses random Gaussian initialization and constant-step-size SGD on ReLU networks, including MNIST and CIFAR-10; reports loss and Hessian-related quantities rather than training classification error. Synthetic runs use 10,000 repetitions; real-dataset experiments use 10 repetitions.
record.method_sensitivity: Synthetic Gauss-10 results distinguish 0% from 15% random labels and use batch sizes 5 and 50; MNIST and CIFAR-10 results vary batch size and network depth, but the text does not report a classification-error comparison.

fits_no_version.finding: Constant-step-size SGD rapidly drives cross-entropy loss toward zero on clean Gauss-10 and more slowly toward zero with 15% uniform label replacement; the authors describe related dynamics on MNIST and CIFAR-10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fully connected ReLU networks trained with constant-step-size SGD exhibit the reported loss-convergence dynamics on synthetic Gaussian classification problems, with qualitatively similar dynamics on MNIST and CIFAR-10.

record.problems: The real-dataset experiments were repeated 10 times, while the 10,000-run distributional characterization applies to synthetic experiments. MNIST and CIFAR-10 loss results are plotted without numerical values in the supplied text. Training classification error is not reported.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant rows identified. Other reported Hessian spectra, subspace overlaps, loss-difference distributions, and generalization-bound quantities do not measure the behavior named in the claim versions.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error in sufficiently large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted labels, and the stated size, stopping and regularization conditions.
Spurious-minimum frequency in two-layer ReLU teacher–student problems and its reduction with one or two extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation with depth in plain batch-normalized convolutional networks; identity-shortcut prevention; and the special-initialization exceptions.
Effects of activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient preservation, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and orthogonal convolution kernels on training speed and trainable depth.
Recovery above the initial linearized stability limit, associated loss increases and curvature drops, divergence conditions, and sustained full-batch behavior at the stability threshold.
Batch normalization's effects on accuracy gain and learning-rate tolerance, and comparable training without normalization using Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Early increases in Hessian eigenvalues or stochastic-gradient norms do not establish V5: no learning rate is compared with a stability threshold, and no catapult or edge-of-stability result is stated. Varying depth without an explicit relevant degradation result does not establish V3. Additional synthetic loss trajectories are outside the listed versions and were already covered by rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted or random labels; model size, stopping, and regularization effects.
Student and teacher widths, spurious-minimum frequency, and the effect of extra student neurons.
Plain versus residual networks, depth effects on training error, and special initialization or normalization comparisons.
Initialization comparisons and their effects on training speed or trainable depth.
Learning rates relative to stability thresholds, curvature changes, and divergence.
Batch normalization effects on training speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

rows.subject: fully connected feed-forward ReLU network trained on Gauss-10
rows.size_stated: 2 hidden layers; [10,30] hidden units; approximately 1,000 parameters
rows.measure: Training loss and stochastic-gradient norm over iterations.
rows.value: SGD converges in less than 50 iterations; both loss and gradient norm converge to zero.
rows.uncertainty: 10,000 runs; quantile trajectories reported, no uncertainty interval stated for this result.
rows.note: This is training-loss behavior, not a reported training classification error.
rows.check: The reported convergence within 50 iterations and loss and gradient norms approaching zero agree with Section 5.1. However, this is a fully connected network on synthetic Gaussian data, so it does not establish any listed version. 'Observed' describes its loss result, not a version's effect.
